descriptionChirho: Basic Qal stem expressing the physical act of crushing, breaking, or bruising something or someone, in active finite and participial forms.
Passive participle describing the condition of being crushed, bruised, or broken, used adjectivally of objects or persons, as in 'a bruised reed.'

labelChirho: be broken, be shattered (Nifal / Qal intransitive)
descriptionChirho: Passive or middle-voice forms expressing that the subject is broken, crushed, or shattered, in Nifal perfects and Qal intransitive imperfects.
Intensive Piel stem conveying deliberate, thorough, or repeated crushing and oppression of persons or things by an agent.
Causative Hifil stem indicating bringing about the crushing or shattering of something, as in Judg 9:53.
Active participle used substantivally to denote those who crush or oppress others, as in Amos 4:1 'you cows of Bashan who crush the needy.'
Passive participle used substantivally to denote oppressed or downtrodden people as a social class, as in Isa 58:6.
Reciprocal Hitpael stem describing mutual jostling, struggling, or pushing against one another, as in Gen 25:22 of Jacob and Esau in the womb.
